headline: the encoder under-2s target has a complete feasible solution that changes no maths: load it to the device once and release the host copy
rediagnosis: about 99 percent of the encoder time is the 63 GB weight transfer, not compute; arithmetic floor is 0.17 s against 3.047 s measured, and 63 GB / 3.047 s = 20.7 GB/s matches the measured 20.0 GB/s pinned H2D
hard_bound: per-call loading makes 3.15 s a hard floor, so under 2 s is physically impossible that way
solution: scheme B: pinned needs only the DiT at 57.7 GiB of a 94.3 GiB limit (36.5 spare) and the device needs 18.97 GiB of 32 (13.03 spare); per-request encoder becomes about 0.5 s
refuted: excluding the vision tower saves only 0.82 GB against a 30.7 GB gap
unverified: current code calls load_to_device and offload_to_cpu in pairs, so releasing the host copy needs a code change
the DiT pinned-master lifetime is not stated
NUMA placement was not recorded when the 20 GB/s was measured
whether the 3.15 s one-off amortises depends on the deployment model
decisions_needed: decide the FP32 guard criterion form
